title: Club Sandwich Breakfast Bake
subtitle: Layered bread, turkey, bacon, tomato, and eggs baked like a strata.
description: Adapted from classic American club sandwich tradition for firehall breakfast bake: layers of toasted bread, turkey, bacon, tomato, and cheddar soaked in an egg-milk custard and baked until puffed and golden for ten portions.

ingredients.name: mayonnaise
ingredients.notes: light spread on bread, plus lettuce after bake

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Club Sandwich Breakfast Bake in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Bacon. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a deep 9x13 pan. Toast bread until crisp and lightly spread one side of each slice with a thin layer of mayonnaise—this keeps layers distinct after baking. Allow 10–15 minutes for mise en place before heat goes on. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cook bacon and prep layers
steps.instruction: Cook bacon until crisp, drain, and crumble. Layer half the bread in the pan, top with half the turkey, bacon, tomato, and Swiss. Repeat layers, finishing with bread on top. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Pour the custard
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs, milk, salt, and pepper until smooth. Pour slowly over the layered bread, pressing gently so custard reaches the bottom. Rest 10 minutes so bread absorbs liquid. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.instruction: Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover, top with remaining Swiss, and bake 15 more until center reaches 165°F and top is golden brown. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Rest and garnish
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares. Top each portion with shredded lettuce and an extra pinch of bacon if desired. Serve with pickle spears at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Toast bread fully crisp—soft bread turns mushy in the custard.
Drain tomato seeds so excess moisture does not pool in the bake.
Cover for the first half of baking so top cheese does not over-brown before center sets.
cleanupNotes: Soak the 9x13 with hot water while warm before egg custard dries on.
Wipe mayo smears from prep boards before they mix with bacon grease.
leftovers: Reheat portions covered at 325°F for 12 minutes; add fresh lettuce after reheating.
Cut leftovers into cubes and pan-fry in butter for crispy breakfast croutons in soup.
